page: Amazon Web Services r6idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are supplemented by 54 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware support for AVX-512 vector instructions and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance does not include a dedicated GPU accelerator.

Memory capacity is configured with 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features 3800 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage, providing fast local input/output capabilities without relying strictly on remote network storage. High-throughput network workloads are supported by a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark outcomes show high throughput in dense multi-core scenarios, scoring in the top 25% for PassMark CPU (57,772.18), multi-core stress-ng (61,937.6), and PassMark database operations (26,521.81). It also achieves strong results in static web serving at 45.56 GB/sec and software compilation with Clang (41,473.0). Conversely, single-core execution profiles fall within the middle 50%, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1700.0 and text processing scores reflecting standard per-thread performance rather than frequency-maximized compute.

Given its substantial DDR4 memory allocation, 100 Gbps networking, and 3.8 TB of bundled NVMe SSD space, the r6idn.16xlarge provides a balanced cost profile for workloads where high data density offsets the need for segregated external storage. The instance is suited for large-scale in-memory caching systems, distributed relational or NoSQL database clusters, real-time analytics engines, and high-bandwidth web serving pipelines.
